question: Should OpenClaw publish and consume fs-safe 0.5.0 now, including the three new public plugin SDK subpaths, or should this migration be narrowed to internal facades until those APIs have separate approval?
rationale: The package publication and lockfile update are necessary for reproducible installation, while the public SDK additions establish an external contract that cannot be selected safely by automated repair alone.

options.title: Publish, lock, and approve the SDK seams
options.body: Publish the exact reviewed fs-safe artifact, regenerate both lock artifacts, and explicitly approve the archive, root-walk, and secret-file plugin contracts before a refreshed validation pass.

options.title: Keep the migration internal
options.body: Retain only internal fs-safe facade use and remove or defer the three public plugin SDK subpaths until a dedicated plugin API proposal is accepted.

options.title: Pause the migration
options.body: Defer the broad dependency upgrade if release timing or public SDK ownership cannot be confirmed now.

recommendation.title: Publish, lock, and approve the SDK seams
recommendation.body: Publish the exact reviewed fs-safe artifact, regenerate both lock artifacts, and explicitly approve the archive, root-walk, and secret-file plugin contracts before a refreshed validation pass.

likelyOwner.reason: This person owns the current integration branch and the referenced upstream fs-safe change, so they are the closest technical routing point for the publication and contract decision.
